2011_020_051711spmtg.paragraph: Agenda packet for a special Troy Board of Education meeting held Tuesday, May 17, 2011 at 6:00 p.m. in the Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098. The board was asked to issue two-year probationary administrative contracts without tenure to three appointees: Timothy Fulcher as Principal of Smith Middle School, Merri Lynn Colligan as Director of Technology, and Katherine Jagels as Director of Special Education. The packet also carries a Section 624 resolution expressing support for the proposed Oakland Intermediate School District budget, and a resolution to enter closed session for the superintendent's evaluation.
2011_020_051711spmtg.page:
**Meeting**
Special Board of Education meeting, Tuesday, May 17, 2011, 6:00 p.m., Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098; district telephone 248.823.4000. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m., and viewable at www.troy.k12.mi.us/tsdnews/video.htm.

**Agenda order**
Pledge of Allegiance; Recognition; Additions & Deletions; Public Communication (agenda items); General - Consent Agenda; Personnel (three considerations); Curriculum; Business; Public Communication (non-agenda items); Other; Closed Session; Adjournment. Public participation is limited to one-half hour for agenda items and one-half hour for non-agenda items, three minutes per speaker.

**Personnel - administrative appointments**

| Item | Appointee | Position | Effective |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.A. | Timothy Fulcher | Principal, Smith Middle School | July 1, 2011 |
| 6.B. | Merri Lynn Colligan | Director of Technology | June 1, 2011, or as soon as possible thereafter |
| 6.C. | Katherine Jagels | Director of Special Education | July 1, 2011 |

Each recommendation carries the same suggested resolution language: a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure in the administrative position.

Fulcher came to Troy from Hazel Park Schools in June 2008, having served Hazel Park first as a math teacher and later as principal of Webb Elementary School; he was hired by the Troy School District as Assistant Principal at Boulan Park Middle School in June of 2008 and was appointed Interim Principal of Smith Middle School in November of 2010. Colligan comes from Southfield Public Schools, where she held the position of Director of Technology for the past six years; she received a Bachelor of Science degree in Education from the University of Michigan in 1995 and is certified in Altiris, Cisco and NCS. Jagels was hired as a teacher in the Troy School District in August of 1977, became an Integration Consultant with Special Education in 1992, and later became Supervisor of Special Education in 2004.

**Business - Oakland Intermediate School District budget**
Item 8.A. asks the board to adopt a resolution under Section 624 of the Revised School Code, as amended, which requires the intermediate school board to submit its proposed budget to each constituent district board no later than May 1 of each year, and requires each constituent board, not later than June 1, to review that budget, adopt a resolution expressing support or disapproval, and submit any specific objections and proposed changes. The resolution states that the Troy Board of Education has received and reviewed the proposed intermediate school district budget and expresses its support, while stating the board's belief that the Intermediate School District is responsible for its own operations, including adoption of its budget, and that Troy's support is for the sole purpose of complying with Section 624. The secretary or designee is directed to forward a copy of the resolution to the intermediate school board or its superintendent no later than June 1, 2011, and all conflicting resolutions are rescinded. A secretary's certification follows, attesting that the resolution was adopted at a meeting held May 17, 2011 and that notice was given under the Open Meetings Act, 1976 PA 267, as amended.

**Closed session**
Item 11.A. asks the board to resolve, as permitted by the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(a), to go into closed session to discuss the superintendent's evaluation. No additional business would take place after that point other than adjournment. The roll call sheet lists Malven, Miletti, Philippart, Underwood, Edmunds, Fleming and Hauff.
2011_020_051711spmtg.verbose:
Board agenda packet for a Special Board of Education Meeting of the Troy School District, Troy, Michigan, held Tuesday, May 17, 2011 at 6:00 p.m. at the Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. The masthead carries the district address (4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098), telephone 248.823.4000, and the district web site www.troy.k12.mi.us, and notes that Board of Education meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m., and can also be viewed online at www.troy.k12.mi.us/tsdnews/video.htm.

AGENDA. The order of business is: 1. Pledge of Allegiance; 2. Recognition; 3. Additions & Deletions; 4. Public Communication (Agenda Items); 5. General - Consent Agenda; 6. Personnel, comprising A. Consideration: Administrative Appointment - Principal, Smith Middle School, B. Consideration: Administrative Appointment - Director of Technology, and C. Consideration: Administrative Appointment - Director of Special Education; 7. Curriculum; 8. Business, comprising A. Consideration: Approve Oakland Intermediate School District Budget; 9. Public Communication (Non-Agenda Items); 10. Other; 11. Closed Session, comprising A. Consideration: Superintendent's Evaluation; and 12. Adjournment. A footnote states that all meetings except closed sessions are open to the public, that the public participation portion is limited to one-half hour for discussion of agenda items and one-half hour for non-agenda items, and that each person is allowed to speak for up to three minutes except where the number of speakers exceeds the time limit, in which case the President may reduce the time limit for each speaker in order to accommodate all individuals wishing to address the board; in any event no one's right to address the board will be denied.

ITEM 6.A. - PERSONNEL - ADMINISTRATIVE APPOINTMENT, PRINCIPAL, SMITH MIDDLE SCHOOL. The superintendent recommends the appointment of Mr. Timothy Fulcher to the position of Principal, Smith Middle School. Mr. Fulcher came to Troy from Hazel Park Schools in June 2008. He served Hazel Park Schools first as a math teacher and later as the principal of Webb Elementary School. Mr. Fulcher was hired by the Troy School District as the Assistant Principal to Boulan Park Middle School in June of 2008, and he was appointed Interim Principal to Smith Middle School in November of 2010. With board approval, Mr. Fulcher will begin his duties as Principal, Smith Middle School effective July 1, 2011. The suggested resolution, with blanks for the mover and supporter and for Ayes and Nays, reads that the Board of Education issues a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure in the administrative position to Mr. Timothy Fulcher, who will begin his duties as Principal, Smith Middle School, effective July 1, 2011.

ITEM 6.B. - PERSONNEL - ADMINISTRATIVE APPOINTMENT, DIRECTOR OF TECHNOLOGY. The superintendent recommends the appointment of Merri Lynn Colligan to the position of Director of Technology. Ms. Colligan comes to Troy from the Southfield Public Schools, where she has held the position of Director of Technology for the past six years. She received a Bachelor of Science degree in Education from the University of Michigan in 1995 and is also certified in Altiris, Cisco and NCS. With board approval, Ms. Merri Lynn Colligan will begin her duties as Director of Technology effective June 1, 2011, or as soon as possible thereafter. The suggested resolution issues a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure in the administrative position to Ms. Colligan with the same effective date language.

ITEM 6.C. - PERSONNEL - ADMINISTRATIVE APPOINTMENT, DIRECTOR OF SPECIAL EDUCATION. The superintendent recommends the appointment of Katherine Jagels to the position of Director of Special Education. Ms. Jagels was hired as a teacher in the Troy School District in August of 1977. She became an Integration Consultant with Special Education in 1992 and later became Supervisor of Special Education in 2004. With board approval, Ms. Katherine Jagels will begin her duties as Director of Special Education effective July 1, 2011. The suggested resolution issues a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure in the administrative position to Ms. Jagels effective July 1, 2011.

ITEM 8.A. - BUSINESS - APPROVE OAKLAND INTERMEDIATE SCHOOL DISTRICT BUDGET. The narrative states that in accordance with Section 624 of the Revised School Code, as amended, the Troy Board of Education is required to review the proposed Oakland Intermediate School District budget and express either its support or disapproval of this budget. The recommended action is adoption of a resolution whose whereas clauses recite, first, that Section 624 of the Revised School Code, as amended, requires the intermediate school board to submit its proposed budget no later than May 1 of each year to the board of each constituent district for review; and second, that not later than June 1 of each year the board of each constituent district shall review the proposed intermediate school district budget, shall adopt a board resolution expressing its support for or disapproval of the proposed intermediate school district budget, and shall submit to the intermediate school board any specific objections and proposed changes the constituent district board has to the budget.

The resolved clauses state: (1) the Troy Board of Education has received and reviewed the proposed intermediate school district budget in accordance with Section 624 of the Revised School Code, as amended, and by adoption of the resolution expresses its support for the proposed intermediate school district budget; the Troy School District Board of Education believes that it is the responsibility of the Intermediate School District to be responsible for its own operations, including adoption of its budget, and the Troy School District's support of the Oakland Intermediate School District's budget is for the sole purpose of complying with Section 624 of the Revised School Code; (2) the secretary of the Troy Board of Education or his/her designee shall forward a copy of this resolution to the intermediate school board or its superintendent no later than June 1, 2011; and (3) all resolutions insofar as they conflict with this resolution are rescinded. Lines follow for Ayes and Nays and the notation 'Resolution declared adopted,' with a signature line for the Secretary, Troy Board of Education. A certification block states that the undersigned duly qualified and acting Secretary of the Board of Education of the Troy School District, Michigan, certifies that the foregoing is a true and complete copy of a resolution adopted by the Troy Board of Education at a meeting held on May 17, 2011, the original of which is part of the board's minutes, and further certifies that notice of the meeting was given to the public under the Open Meetings Act, 1976 PA 267, as amended.

ITEM 11.A. - CLOSED SESSION - SUPERINTENDENT'S EVALUATION. The packet states that the board must pass a resolution to go into closed session for the purpose of discussing the superintendent's evaluation, that following passage of the resolution the Board of Education will go into closed session, and that no additional business will take place after that time other than to officially adjourn the meeting. The suggested resolution reads that, as permitted in the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(a), the Troy Board of Education shall go into closed session to discuss the superintendent's evaluation. A roll call vote is directed, with the names listed in order: Malven, Miletti, Philippart, Underwood, Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff.

2011_021_051811spmtg.paragraph: Special meeting agenda packet for the Troy School District Board of Trustees, May 18, 2011 at 6:00 p.m. at the Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098, with a single item of business: ratification of the tentative agreement with the Troy Education Association/MEA/NEA. The two-year contract runs August 15, 2011 through June 30, 2013 and provides no salary schedule increase and a salary schedule step freeze in both the 2011/2012 and 2012/2013 school years, along with MESSA Choices plan changes and caps on the district's annual MESSA PAK premium contribution. Attached are the negotiated 2011/2012 and 2012/2013 school-year calendars.
2011_021_051811spmtg.page:
**Meeting**
Special meeting of the Board of Trustees, Troy School District, May 18, 2011, beginning at 6:00 PM at the Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. Agenda: 1. Pledge of Allegiance; 2. Public Communication; 3. Personnel - A. Consideration: Troy Education Association (TEA) Contract Ratification; 4. Adjournment. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. (except in July and August).

**Item 3.A. - TEA contract ratification**
A tentative agreement between representatives of the Troy Board of Education and the Troy Education Association/MEA/NEA (TEA) was reached on May 13, 2011, and the TEA membership voted to ratify it on May 17, 2011. The agreement is a two-year contract for the period August 15, 2011 through June 30, 2013. Terms: no salary schedule increase for the 2011/2012 and 2012/2013 school years; a salary schedule step freeze for both years; and cost-sharing between TSD and the TEA of the total compensation for the full-time release TEA President. The teachers' insurance plan, MESSA Choices, will be changed to add a $300/$600 in-network deductible, a $10/$40 prescription drug card, and $10 office visit co-pays, effective no later than July 1, 2011.

Maximum annual district payment toward a teacher's total MESSA PAK premium (medical, prescription drug, vision, dental, life, and long-term disability), for both 2011/2012 and 2012/2013:

| Coverage tier | Maximum district payment |
| --- | --- |
| Single | $6,500 |
| Two-person | $14,600 |
| Full family | $16,250 |

Any remaining premium cost for MESSA PAK coverage is paid by teachers electing such coverage on a pre-tax basis through payroll deduction. The suggested resolution ratifies and adopts the tentative agreement for the period August 15, 2011 through June 30, 2013.

**Attached calendars**
2011/2012: staff first reporting day August 31, 2011; student first day September 6, 2011; last student day June 15, 2012. Marking periods end November 4, 2011 (9 weeks), January 26, 2012 (10 weeks), April 12, 2012 (10 weeks) and June 15, 2012 (9 weeks); progress reports due October 10, 2011, December 12, 2011, March 12, 2012 and May 21, 2012. Winter recess begins December 19, 2011, mid-winter recess February 20, 2012, spring recess April 2, 2012.

2012/2013: staff first reporting day August 29, 2012; student first day September 4, 2012; last student day June 14, 2013. Marking periods end November 2, 2012 (9 weeks), January 25, 2013 (10 weeks), April 11, 2013 (10 weeks) and June 14, 2013 (9 weeks); progress reports due October 8, 2012, December 10, 2012, March 11, 2013 and May 20, 2013. A note states that due to potential modification of the county-wide calendar for the 2012-2013 school year, both parties agree the 2012-2013 calendar may be adjusted via mutual agreement.

Both calendars total 184 teacher days and 179 student days, with 10 high school half days, 8 middle school half days and 8 elementary half days. Twelve hours of professional development count as student instructional hours, including 6 hours of collaborative time already incorporated through the school year and 6 hours in August/September.

2011_022_060711regmtg.paragraph: Regular Board of Education meeting agenda packet for Tuesday, June 7, 2011 at 7:00 p.m. at Athens High School, 4333 John R, Troy, MI 48085, dominated by an end-of-year recognition program running from item 2.A. through 2.SS. and covering All-State winter athletes, 66 senior scholar athletes, and dozens of academic and arts competitions. The board was also asked to add and then ratify the TESPA contract, a two-year agreement for July 1, 2010 through June 30, 2012 carrying economic concessions exceeding 2.5% in compensation and a move to the district's self-funded PPO plan.
2011_022_060711regmtg.page:
**Meeting**
Board of Education Meeting, Tuesday, June 7, 2011, 7:00 p.m., Athens High School, 4333 John R, Troy, MI 48085. Agenda: 1. Pledge of Allegiance; 2. Recognition (items A through SS); 3. Additions & Deletions; 4. Public Communication (agenda items); 5. Personnel - A. TESPA Contract Ratification; 6. Curriculum; 7. Business - A. Food Service Management Contract for 2011/2012 and B. Resolution to Hold a Public Hearing on the Proposed 2011/2012 School Year Budget; 8. Public Communication (non-agenda items); 9. Other; 10. Closed Session - A. Negotiations; 11. Adjournment.

**Recognition program**
The listed recognitions include All-State Athletes (Winter Sports); Senior Scholar Athletes (Winter and Spring Sports); Chess Championship (Barnard/Baker); Destination ImagiNation/Troy Creative Minds (Leonard/Larson); Michigan Green School Awards; Thinking Cap Quiz Bowl (Barnard/Baker/Boulan Park); Midwest Talent Search (Barnard/Baker/Boulan Park/Larson/Smith); Perfect ACT/Explore Score (Baker, Boulan, Larson, Smith); 2011 MSBOA All-State Honors Band (Baker/Boulan Park/Smith); Michigan Color Guard (Baker); Boulan Park Advanced Orchestra; Celebration of Young Poets Contest (Boulan Park); American Mathematics Competition 8 (Boulan Park/Smith); Michigan Mathematics League Competition, National Math Counts Competition, National Anthology of Poetry by Young Americans, 2011 Scholastic Challenge (Boulan Park); National Language Arts League (Boulan Park/Larson); Science Olympiad (Troy High); WordMasters Challenge (Boulan Park/Larson/Smith); Larson 8th Grade Orchestra; Future Problem Solving Competition (Larson); Ford Freedom Essay Contest (Smith); Federal Challenge, Japanese Quiz Bowl, Japanese Speech Contest, Japanese Video Contest, Model UN Competition and Scholastic Arts Awards (Athens); National Merit Scholarships (Athens/Troy High); Advanced Placement Scholars; DECA Career Development Conference, French Exam, Intel International Science & Engineering Fair, Gladiator Yearbook Awards, China Quiz Bowl, Michigan Brain Bee, MSVMA State Solo and Ensemble, Michigan Association of Student Councils and Honor Society, NASA DIME Competition, National Biology Competition, Siemens Challenge and Southeastern Highland Games (Troy High); and Troy High School band and orchestra music festivals including the Dixie Classic Music Festival, Michigan Youth Arts Festival and MSBO State Solo and Ensemble Festival.

Mr. Jolly was to read biographies of the All-State athletes, most of them synchronized swimmers coached by Lori Uchwal. Senior scholar athletes number 66 from winter and spring sports; the distinction requires maintaining a 3.5 cumulative grade point average while participating in an athletic program.

**Item 3.A. / 5.A. - TESPA contract ratification**
Item 3.A. adds Item 5.A., TESPA Contract Ratification, to the agenda under Personnel. A tentative agreement between representatives of the Troy Board of Education and the Troy Educational Support Personnel Association/MEA/NEA (TESPA) was reached on May 25, 2011, and the TESPA membership voted to ratify it on June 3, 2011. The agreement is a two-year contract for the period July 1, 2010 through June 30, 2012. It provides no salary schedule increase for the 2010/2011 or 2011/2012 school years and a salary schedule step freeze for the 2011/2012 school year. It also includes economic concessions which exceed 2.5% in compensation for TESPA members and a change in the insurance plan for TESPA members to the self-funded PPO plan provided for administrative and non-represented employees, with accompanying employee premium contributions.

**Closed session**
Item 10.A. asks the board to resolve, as permitted in the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(a), to go into closed session to discuss negotiations, after which no additional business will take place other than adjournment. Roll call names listed: Miletti, Philippart, Underwood, Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Malven.

**Meeting**
Special Board of Education Meeting, Tuesday, June 14, 2011, convening following the Board Workshop, Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098; district telephone 248.823.4000. Agenda: 1. Pledge of Allegiance; 2. Recognition; 3. Additions & Deletions - A. Addition of Item 6.B. under Personnel for TESA Contract Ratification; 4. Public Communication (agenda items); 5. General - Consent Agenda; 6. Personnel - A. Administrative Appointment, Morse Elementary School and B. Troy Education Secretarial Association (TESA) Contract Ratification; 7. Curriculum; 8. Business; 9. Public Communication (non-agenda items); 10. Other; 11. Closed Session - A. Negotiations; 12. Adjournment.

**Item 6.A. - Principal, Morse Elementary School**
The superintendent recommends Stephanie Acord as Principal of Morse Elementary School, effective July 1, 2011, under a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure. Background: Principal of Taft-Galloway Elementary School in the Wayne-Westland Community School District for the past seven years; previously with Crestwood School District in Dearborn Heights as an Elementary (K-8) Science Instructional Specialist for 2 1/2 years and a 3rd and 4th grade teacher for 2 years; and a year as a kindergarten teacher in the Detroit Public Schools. She received an Educational Specialist degree in Educational Leadership from Eastern Michigan University in August of 2010 and holds a current Professional Education Certificate with endorsements in Elementary K-5, Early Childhood Education and Science (6-8), as well as an Administrator Certificate for both Elementary and Secondary Administration.

**Items 3.A. and 6.B. - TESA contract ratification**
Item 3.A. adds Item 6.B., TESA Contract Ratification, to the agenda under Personnel. A tentative agreement between representatives of the Troy Board of Education and the Troy Educational Secretaries Association/MEA/NEA (TESA) was reached on June 9, 2011; the TESA membership voted to ratify it on June 13, 2011. The agreement is a two-year contract for July 1, 2011 through June 30, 2013, providing a wage schedule reduction and step freeze for the 2011/2012 and 2012/2013 school years. Overall it includes economic concessions which exceed 8.5% in compensation for TESA members and a change in the insurance plan. MESSA Choices will be changed to add a $500/$1000 in-network deductible, a $10/$40 prescription drug card, and $20 office visit co-pays.

Maximum annual district payment toward a secretary's total MESSA PAK insurance premium, for both 2011/2012 and 2012/2013:

| Coverage tier | Maximum district payment |
| --- | --- |
| Single | $6,700 |
| Two-person | $14,800 |
| Full family | $16,500 |

Any remaining premium cost of MESSA PAK coverage is paid by the secretaries electing such coverage on a pre-tax basis through payroll deduction.

**Closed session**
Item 11.A. asks the board to resolve, as permitted in the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(a), to go into closed session to discuss negotiations, with no additional business after that point other than adjournment. Roll call names listed: Philippart, Underwood, Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Malven, Miletti.

ITEM 6.A. - PERSONNEL - ADMINISTRATIVE APPOINTMENT, PRINCIPAL, MORSE ELEMENTARY SCHOOL. The superintendent recommends the appointment of Stephanie Acord to the position of Principal, Morse Elementary School. Ms. Acord comes to Troy from the Wayne-Westland Community School District, where she has held the position of Principal, Taft-Galloway Elementary School for the past seven years. Ms. Acord previously worked for the Crestwood School District in Dearborn Heights, where she was an Elementary (K-8) Science Instructional Specialist for 2 1/2 years and a 3rd and 4th grade teacher for 2 years. She also spent a year as a Kindergarten teacher in the Detroit Public Schools. Ms. Acord received an Educational Specialist degree in Educational Leadership from Eastern Michigan University in August of 2010. She also possesses both a current Professional Education Certificate with endorsements in Elementary K-5, Early Childhood Education and Science (6-8), as well as an Administrator Certificate for both Elementary and Secondary Administration. With board approval, Ms. Stephanie Acord will begin her duties as Principal of Morse Elementary School effective July 1, 2011. The recommended action is acceptance of a suggested resolution, with blanks for the mover and seconder and for Ayes and Nays, providing that the Board of Education issues a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure in the administrative position to Ms. Stephanie Acord, who will begin her duties as Principal, Morse Elementary School effective July 1, 2011.

ITEM 3.A. - ADDITIONS & DELETIONS - TESA CONTRACT RATIFICATION. The recommended action is adoption of a resolution that Item 6.B., TESA Contract Ratification, be added to the evening's agenda under the Personnel section, with blanks for mover, supporter, Ayes and Nays.

ITEM 6.B. - PERSONNEL - TESA CONTRACT RATIFICATION. A tentative agreement between representatives of the Troy Board of Education and the Troy Educational Secretaries Association/MEA/NEA (TESA) was reached on June 9, 2011. The TESA membership voted to ratify the agreement on June 13, 2011. The tentative agreement is a two-year contract for the period of July 1, 2011 through June 30, 2013. It provides a wage schedule reduction and step freeze for the 2011/2012 and 2012/2013 school years. Overall, the tentative agreement includes economic concessions which exceed 8.5% in compensation for TESA members and a change in the insurance plan for TESA members. The secretaries' insurance plan, MESSA Choices, will be changed to include the addition of a $500/$1000 in-network deductible, a $10/$40 prescription drug card, and $20 office visit co-pays. In addition, the maximum annual amount the district will pay toward a secretary's total MESSA PAK insurance premium for both the 2011/2012 and 2012/2013 school years will be as follows: $6,700 for single coverage, $14,800 for two-person coverage, and $16,500 for full family coverage. Any remaining premium cost of the MESSA PAK coverage will be paid by the secretaries electing such coverage on a pre-tax basis through payroll deduction. The recommended action is acceptance of a suggested resolution, with blanks for mover, supporter, Ayes and Nays, providing that the Board of Education ratifies and adopts the tentative agreement reached on June 9, 2011 between representatives of the Troy Board of Education and the Troy Educational Secretaries Association/MEA/NEA (TESA) for the period of July 1, 2011 through June 30, 2013.

ITEM 11.A. - CLOSED SESSION - NEGOTIATIONS. The packet states that the board must pass a resolution to go into closed session for the purpose of discussing negotiations, that following passage of the resolution the Board of Education will go into closed session, and that no additional business will take place after that time other than to officially adjourn the meeting. The suggested resolution provides that, as permitted in the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(a), the Troy Board of Education shall go into closed session to discuss negotiations. A roll call vote is directed, with the trustee names listed in order: Philippart, Underwood, Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Malven, Miletti.

Taken together, the packet records two personnel actions on the same evening: the hiring of an outside candidate into an elementary principalship under the district's standard two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure, and the ratification of the secretaries' bargaining agreement, which unlike a simple freeze carries an outright wage schedule reduction alongside the step freeze and the shift in health plan design and premium-cap structure.
